subject: physics
question_text: Can a substance contract on heating? Give an example.

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2023 (Q8) — Section A, 2 marks. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced from that paper. Physics hand-checked: water contracts when heated from 0 °C to 4 °C, where its coefficient of expansion is negative and its density is maximum at 4 °C; rubber is a second standard example of contraction on heating. Above 4 °C water expands in the ordinary way.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Yes, it can
lines: Yes. A few substances contract when they
are heated over a certain range of
The coefficient of expansion is negative
steps.margin_note: First mark. The word yes together with the reason earns it.
steps.why: Expansion coefficients are positive for almost every material, but nothing forbids a negative one. A negative coefficient simply means the volume falls as the temperature rises.
common_mistakes: Answering only no. The anomalous behaviour of water is the standard counter-example.

recall.must_convey: That yes, a substance can contract on heating, because its coefficient of expansion is negative in that range.
reject: water from zero to four degrees

steps.memory_tip: Contraction on heating simply means a negative coefficient of expansion.

steps.label: The example
lines: Heating water from 0 °C to 4 °C makes its
volume decrease and its density rise.
Above 4 °C water expands in the ordinary
way. Rubber also contracts on heating.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name water and give the range 0 °C to 4 °C.
steps.why: Between 0 °C and 4 °C the open structure left over from ice keeps collapsing as the water warms, so the volume falls until 4 °C is reached.
common_mistakes: Writing that water contracts on heating at every temperature. Above 4 °C it expands normally.

recall.must_convey: That water contracts when heated from 0 °C to 4 °C.
accept: water from zero to four degrees

steps.memory_tip: Water is densest at 4 °C. From 0 °C up to 4 °C it shrinks, not grows.

insider_note: A one word answer plus one example — the range 0 °C to 4 °C is what the examiner looks for, not the word water alone.
